That's the version we installed yesterday, and today our desk staff noticed text from restricted clinical notes in patient-search previews. The full note still refuses to open under their accounts, but the opening lines are displayed below the patient's name before they click anything. We reproduced it using a test record and a reception-only login. Nobody changed that account's permissions. Can you check what changed in 4.9.2? The desk team shouldn't get a sneak peek at something the app then tells them they aren't permitted to view.

report.title: Help drawer covers the booking controls
report.description: The reception-role check is fine here: patient-search previews do not show the first lines of restricted clinical notes, and reception cannot open those notes either. That's not the issue I'm reporting. My complaint is that the in-app help drawer covers the booking form's bottom controls on our small desk monitor. It also has no visible close button at that window size, so staff have to widen the browser every time they accidentally open help.

report.title: Editing a home-exercise plan wipes the completion history
report.description:
Pasting this over from our clinic channel because we've now seen it with three patients at Mosswick Physio.

Our patient Nella Brindle had been ticking off her exercises every day since Monday. This morning I opened her existing home-exercise plan, changed the repetitions on the calf raises, and added one balance exercise. I left the other four exercises in place. After saving, the completion ticks from earlier in the week were gone for those four exercises too. The patient app and our clinician view now make it look like she hasn't done any of them.

She showed me a screenshot taken before the appointment, so this isn't just her remembering incorrectly. It had several days marked complete. The exercises are still there with the same names, and I haven't discharged her or created a separate plan.

I tried it with our fictional training patient as well: mark two exercises complete, open the plan, change the instructions on one, then save. Both lose their earlier ticks, including the one I didn't touch. Ticking something off after the change works, but that only gives us a new mark; it doesn't bring back the earlier ones.

We need to adjust programmes as people progress without losing the record of what they already did. For now I've asked the team not to make changes midweek, which isn't a workable long-term approach. Can you check whether those earlier completions are recoverable?

report.title: One small routine tweak makes last week's green badges vanish
report.description: A patient had five days of green 'done' badges beside her movements. I increased the hold time for just one movement in her routine and hit Save. When we opened the calendar again, every day before today looked blank, even beside movements I hadn't touched. The patient thought we'd thrown away all her hard work. Can we adjust the instructions without making her previous effort disappear?

report.title: Old ticks gone after a plan change
report.description: The exercises we kept now have no past completion ticks after we changed the plan.

report.title: Release 6.8.2 is clearing our patients' exercise progress
report.description:
I think the TendrelStep 6.8.2 release has broken this. Since we noticed the new release banner, modifying a patient's home-exercise plan makes their earlier completed days disappear.

Today I only changed the sets on one exercise. Two other exercises stayed exactly as they were, but their completion ticks vanished as well. Yesterday's work showed up before I saved and was blank afterwards. The patient can record today's exercises normally, so it seems specifically to affect anything logged before the update to the plan.

Please roll back whatever changed in 6.8.2. We use those marks during reviews and now can't tell who actually missed a day.

report.title: Exercise history is fine; favourites need alphabetical sorting
report.description:
To be clear, editing a home-exercise plan does NOT reset adherence history for us. Previously recorded completion ticks stay visible, including for exercises that remain in the plan. That part works fine.

My complaint is about the exercise-library favourites list: it stays in the order we added items, and there's no way to sort it alphabetically. We've got dozens of favourites now, so finding one during an appointment means scrolling through the whole list. Could we get an A–Z option?

report.title: Waitlist sends follow-up offers to people needing an initial assessment
report.description: We added someone to the TendrelStep waitlist for a 60-minute initial assessment with their preferred therapist. A 20-minute follow-up slot opened within their available hours, and they received an automated offer for it. The therapist and time were right, but the appointment type was wrong. Reception had to explain that we couldn't fit their first assessment into that gap. Can the waitlist check the requested appointment type before sending an offer?

report.title: First-visit queue is picking up return-visit gaps
report.description: A new client joined our cancellation queue for a one-hour intake. When a twenty-minute return visit came free, TendrelStep texted them a link to take it. It was with the right practitioner and inside the hours they'd said they could come, but it wasn't the service they'd put their name down for. We need the queue to distinguish a first visit from a return visit, not just find an opening in the diary.

report.title: Wrong kind of visit in waitlist text
report.description: Someone waiting for a full first assessment got a waitlist offer for a brief follow-up instead.

report.title: Build 5.8.14 seems to have broken waitlist appointment types
report.description:
Flagging this as a possible regression in TendrelStep build 5.8.14, which we installed yesterday. Reception thinks the new release has stopped respecting the visit type when it sends cancellation offers.

This morning we had a new patient on the waitlist for a 60-minute initial assessment. Their entry specified that service, the clinician they wanted, and weekday mornings. An existing patient's 15-minute follow-up was cancelled with the same clinician at 10:15. The new patient immediately received a text inviting them to take that opening.

They called us because the link described a follow-up, and they have never attended our clinic before. We checked the waitlist entry rather than relying on what they'd told us: it still says initial assessment. Nobody at the desk changed it or manually sent the invitation. The clinician and the morning window both line up, so it looks as though those parts are being checked while the service selection isn't.

I initially blamed yesterday's build because that's when we started paying attention to this. However, another receptionist found a saved message from last week, before the update, where somebody needing an initial assessment was also sent a short follow-up opening. So perhaps the release timing is a coincidence.

For now we're checking every cancellation manually before letting the queue run. We can't ask a clinician to squeeze a full assessment into fifteen minutes, and the texts make clients think we've found them a suitable visit.

report.title: Waitlist is fine; receipt list needs amount sorting
report.description: The automated waitlist offers are working correctly for us now. Patients requesting a long initial assessment are not receiving short follow-up slots, and the requested appointment type is being respected alongside therapist and availability. This ticket is about the receipt screen instead: we can't sort receipts by total amount. Reception needs to review the largest payments first, but clicking the Amount heading does nothing and there's no sort option in the menu.

report.title: Discharged patients still included in active caseload
report.description:
Our TendrelStep dashboard says therapist Nelvi has 38 active patients, but nine of those have already been discharged. Their individual records all show Discharged, with the correct end dates, so reception hasn't forgotten to finish their episodes.

We tried archiving one of those nine and the dashboard number immediately dropped to 37. Discharging another patient without archiving them did not reduce the number at all.

We don't normally archive people as soon as treatment ends because we still need easy access for follow-up correspondence. Surely a discharged patient shouldn't count toward a therapist's current workload just because their record hasn't been archived? At the moment we have to keep a separate tally before deciding who can take new referrals.

report.title: Finished care still pads the workload tiles
report.description: The team overview gives Osvella 24 people to look after. Six have finished treatment, and opening each chart shows “Care complete.” That leaves 18 who are actually coming back. Moving one finished chart into long-term storage brought the tile down to 23; marking someone else's care complete left it unchanged. We need the allocation screen to reflect who still needs appointments, not everyone whose chart is still on the everyday shelf.

report.title: Finished patients still in our workload number
report.description: The active caseload figure still includes people we've discharged but haven't archived.

report.title: Release 6.4.2 seems to have broken the caseload totals
report.description:
Posting this here before our next capacity meeting because I think TendrelStep 6.4.2 has introduced a counting issue. We installed that release on Monday, and this is the first week I've noticed the discrepancy. I can't say whether anyone checked the same figures before the update, but the timing looks suspicious.

At Marnelith Physiotherapy, the overview gives Quenra an active caseload of 46. We went through her list together and found 12 people whose treatment has ended. Every one of those records says Discharged. The dates are right, and nobody has reopened their care. There are no future appointments for them either.

We initially thought the page was showing yesterday's figures, so we left it overnight. This morning it still said 46. Refreshing and having another staff member open the overview gave the same result.

Reception then archived two of the discharged records as a test. The figure changed to 44 straight away. We discharged a different person after their final session, leaving their record unarchived, and the figure stayed at 44. So the discharge label seems to save properly; it just doesn't affect the number we're using for workload planning.

Please don't tell us to archive everyone as a workaround. Some finished patients still have correspondence pending, and our staff want those records readily available. The two test records can stay archived, but doing that for everyone would change our normal workflow.

Could someone check whether the new release changed this screen? We're being asked to distribute new referrals using these totals, and Quenra looks much busier than she really is.

report.title: Caseload counts are fine; invoice footer is getting cut off
report.description:
Just to separate this from the earlier dashboard discussion: our active caseload counts are correct. Discharged patients are not inflating the totals, and we aren't having to manually archive them to make the numbers right.

My ticket is about the payment instructions at the bottom of printed invoices. The last two lines are cut off on paper even though they're visible in the preview. We shortened the footer and it prints, but we'd like to keep the full instructions. This happens with ordinary invoices, not insurer claims or treatment-plan PDFs.

report.title: Patient signature missing from signed treatment-plan PDF
report.description:
Support ticket from reception: We need help with the treatment-plan PDFs we download from patient records in TendrelStep. The patient has signed the plan, and the record shows it as signed with the correct signature timestamp, but their signature image is missing from the downloaded PDF. The clinician's signature is still there.

We noticed this when preparing a copy for someone who wanted to take their plan home. The patient signature area was empty, so reception assumed we had forgotten to collect it. We reopened the record and checked: the signed status was present, the date and time matched the appointment, and we could see the patient's handwriting in the app.

We downloaded the document again from the same record. Same result. We also opened the file on another reception computer to rule out a display issue. The patient signature area was still blank, while the clinician signature appeared normally. This is not a case where the whole signing section has disappeared; the labels and signing details remain visible.

We have now checked two other recently completed plans and found the same discrepancy. Please don't ask us to have everyone sign again without first checking the document generation. As far as we can tell, the signatures were collected successfully and are still available in the records.

For now we have stopped handing out these PDFs because they make completed plans look incomplete. Can you investigate why the patient signature doesn't carry through and confirm whether we can regenerate the existing plans once it is fixed?

report.title: Take-home care agreement loses the client's handwriting
report.description: The person receiving care draws their name on the tablet and we can still see that scribble in TendrelStep afterward. The screen says the agreement is complete and shows when they accepted it. But when we save the printable copy to send home, the space for their handwritten mark is empty. Our physio's own mark comes through normally. It looks like the take-home copy isn't picking up what the client drew, even though the app clearly has it.

report.title: Only the patient signature is blank
report.description: Treatment-plan PDF says the patient signed and shows when, but their signature is blank; the clinician's is there.

report.title: Think 5.14.2 broke the signed plan downloads
report.description: Flagging this as a possible regression in TendrelStep 5.14.2 because that's the release number we noticed when this started. Our treatment plans still show the patient as signed, complete with a signature timestamp, and their signature is visible when we open the record. Download the PDF, though, and the patient's signature box is empty. The treating physio's signature prints correctly. I tried downloading an older signed plan as well and got the same blank patient box. My guess is the latest release changed the layout, but that's just based on when reception first spotted it.

report.title: Signed PDFs are fine; emailed copy has an uneditable subject
report.description: The treatment-plan PDF is not missing the patient's signature here. Both patient and clinician signatures appear correctly, along with the signed status and signature timestamp. Our complaint is about sending that PDF: TendrelStep gives the outgoing email the subject 'Your documents' and provides no way to customize it. We'd like to use 'Your treatment plan' so clients can find it later. The attachment itself is complete and looks fine.

report.title: Can't give our two locations different logos
report.description:
We run Mossquay Physio and Brindlefen Rehab as two locations under the same TendrelStep clinic account. They share reception staff and patient records, but each location has its own name and logo. Patients should see the appropriate logo on that location's online booking page and in the reminder header.

Yesterday I opened the Mossquay location, went into settings, and uploaded its green logo. The preview looked right, so I saved it. Our receptionist then checked the Brindlefen booking link and found the same green logo there too. Brindlefen should have the orange one. I uploaded the orange logo while working from Brindlefen, and now Mossquay shows orange as well.

I initially thought I'd accidentally selected both locations. I tried again with only Mossquay selected and had another staff member check the public pages from a separate browser. Same result: whichever logo we upload last appears for both sites. The reminder previews also use that last uploaded logo, even when the appointment belongs to the other location.

I've checked the location details screen and the booking-page options, but I can't find anywhere to choose a logo for an individual location. The only upload field seems to apply to the entire clinic account. There isn't an error message; everything saves successfully, just much more broadly than we intended.

Is there a location-specific setting we're missing? We'd rather not split into separate accounts because our team needs the shared diary and records. For now we've put up a plain group logo, but neither branch wants that as the permanent solution. We need each location's booking page and reminder header to keep its own logo without replacing the other one.

report.title: Both venues keep inheriting the same emblem
report.description: Our two practices trade under separate identities but share one TendrelStep workspace. I put the blue bird artwork on the east site's reservation screen, and the west site's screen immediately picked it up too. Replacing it with the west site's sun symbol made the east site show the sun instead. The banners above the appointment texts follow along as well. I can't find an independent artwork picker for either venue. We need the bird for one and the sun for the other, not a single image shared between them.

report.title: Branch logos won't stay separate
report.description: Each branch needs its own logo, but we only seem to get one shared choice for all of them.

report.title: Release 8.14.2 seems to have tied our site logos together
report.description: Flagging this as an 8.14.2 regression because that's the release we were on when we noticed it. We just added our second location and uploaded its logo, which also replaced the logo on the original location's booking page. Switching the original back replaces the new site's logo too, including in reminder headers. I expected the location selector to scope the upload, but there's no separate logo field in either location's details. Can someone check the release? We didn't try separate site logos before this week, so I can't confirm they ever worked independently.

report.title: Logo setup is fine; receipt list sorting is the issue
report.description: The location-specific logo settings are working fine for us now. Changing one location's logo does not change it everywhere, and each booking page and reminder header shows the right branding. This ticket is about the payment receipt list: when I sort by receipt number, it puts R-100 before R-20. Nothing is missing and the amounts are correct, but reception has to hunt through the list because the numbers aren't ordered numerically.

report.title: Tax is a penny higher on invoices with small extras
report.description: Our bookkeeper spotted this on an invoice with three taxable consumables at 0.11 each, taxed at 5%. TendrelStep shows 0.03 tax, but calculating 5% on the 0.33 subtotal gives 0.02 after rounding. It looks like each item's tax gets rounded before being added together. We checked for an invoice setting to calculate tax on the subtotal instead but couldn't find one. These tiny differences are making our daily reconciliation awkward.

unlisted_problem.title: Invoice tax totals round each line instead of the subtotal
unlisted_problem.summary: Invoices containing several low-value taxable items can show a tax total one minor currency unit higher than the clinic's subtotal-based calculation. The invoice calculator rounds tax per line and offers no subtotal-rounding setting.

report.title: Refund completed, but pack session still missing
report.description: Refunded a cancelled visit paid from a six-session pack: the payment value came back, but the pack stayed at five remaining instead of returning to six. Had to add the session back manually.

unlisted_problem.title: Refunds do not replenish prepaid session balances
unlisted_problem.summary: Refunding an appointment paid from a prepaid session pack returns the payment value but leaves the pack's remaining-session count unchanged. Staff must manually restore the consumed session.

report.title: Emergency contact vanished when we merged duplicate records
report.description:
Ticket from reception at Brindlefern Physio: We had two records for the same patient. The older one had the correct appointment history, so we kept that as the main record. Its emergency-contact section was blank. The newer duplicate had the patient's emergency contact, including their relationship and contact details.

After the merge, the appointments were where we expected them, but the emergency-contact section was still completely blank. We only noticed because the clinician checked it before the next visit. Reception had to ask the patient for those details again.

Is there a way to recover the contact from the merged record? We expected an empty section in the retained record to pick up the information from the other one, not lose it.

unlisted_problem.title: Emergency contact removed during patient-record merge
unlisted_problem.summary: Merging a duplicate patient into a primary record with an empty emergency-contact section discards the duplicate's emergency contact. The merge logic treats an empty primary value as authoritative rather than copying the populated value.

report.title: Where can patients request a copy of their records?
report.description: A patient asked how to request their treatment notes through the portal. I logged in with our test patient and couldn't find a request form, submission button, or anywhere to see whether a request is pending. At the moment we're telling people to contact reception, then tracking requests in a separate spreadsheet. Are we overlooking something, or is this not available in TendrelStep?

unlisted_problem.title: Patient portal lacks self-service access-request submission
unlisted_problem.summary: Patients cannot submit a record-access request from the portal. Clinics must receive and track these requests outside the app because no request form or status view exists.

report.title: Can't keyboard out of therapist filter
report.description: Open the calendar's therapist filter using the keyboard and focus gets stuck inside it—Tab just cycles through the menu, Escape does nothing, and someone has to click it closed.

unlisted_problem.title: Keyboard focus becomes trapped in the calendar filter menu
unlisted_problem.summary: Keyboard-only staff cannot leave the therapist filter menu using Tab or Escape once it is expanded. Its focus trap remains active until a pointer user closes the menu.

report.title: Room kiosk is named on every audit entry
report.description:
We need help understanding the audit history for our shared treatment-room device.

Our clinicians use the same kiosk between appointments. Each person unlocks it with their own credentials before opening a patient record. The screen shows the clinician's name after unlocking, so staff have been assuming that edits made during that session would be recorded against that person.

Yesterday we reviewed a change to a treatment note and couldn't tell who had made it. The audit entry named the room kiosk account, not the clinician. We checked several other entries and found the same thing for note edits and changes to exercise plans.

This morning we tested it deliberately with two clinicians. The first unlocked the kiosk, changed a note in our test patient record, and locked it again. The second then unlocked it and made a different change. Both changes appeared in the audit history under the same kiosk account. Neither clinician's name appeared on those entries, even though their names were visible on the device while they worked.

We can sometimes work out who was in the room from the appointment calendar, but that is not reliable when someone covers a colleague or finishes documentation later. We need to know who actually performed each action, rather than which device they happened to use.

Is there a configuration we're missing? If not, please advise whether staff should stop using the shared kiosk for record changes until individual attribution is available. We'd also like to know whether the earlier entries can be clarified without guessing from the rota.

unlisted_problem.title: Audit events identify a shared kiosk rather than the clinician
unlisted_problem.summary: Actions performed after a clinician unlocks a shared treatment-room kiosk are attributed to the kiosk account in the audit log. The unlock identity is not passed to the audit-event writer.

report.title: Exercise steps stay in the clinic language
report.description: A patient switched the home-exercise app to Spanish, which is offered in the language picker. The menus changed, but the written instructions under every assigned exercise stayed in English, our clinic default. They closed and reopened the app, and we reassigned one exercise to check, but nothing changed. The patient can navigate the app now but still can't read the exercise steps.

unlisted_problem.title: Exercise instructions ignore the patient's selected language
unlisted_problem.summary: Text instructions in the home-exercise app remain in the clinic's default language after a patient chooses another supported language. The instruction service does not receive the patient's language preference.

report.title: Minus quantity adds stock through the usage log
report.description: I accidentally entered -3 instead of 3 when recording elastic wrap used during a session. TendrelStep accepted it and our available stock went from 20 to 23. There wasn't a stock-adjustment entry explaining the increase, just the usage row with a negative number. I tried the same thing on a test item and it also saved without a warning. Can negative quantities be blocked here? Reception could unintentionally inflate stock while trying to log what was used.

unlisted_problem.title: Stock usage accepts negative quantities
unlisted_problem.summary: The consumables log allows staff to record a negative quantity used, which increases available stock without a corresponding stock-adjustment event. Quantity validation checks only that the input is numeric.

report.title: Cancelled bookings still showing on subscribed calendar
report.description:
Our clinic manager subscribes to the TendrelStep appointment feed in a separate calendar app. New appointments show up fine, but cancelled ones keep sitting there as if they're still booked.

We cancelled a test appointment yesterday and refreshed the subscription several times. It disappeared from TendrelStep but remained on the subscribed calendar. A newly created test appointment came through during the same period, so the subscription is still updating. Starting a fresh subscription doesn't show the cancelled appointment; it's the existing calendar that won't clear it. Staff are now checking two calendars and getting conflicting availability.

unlisted_problem.title: External calendar events lack cancellation updates
unlisted_problem.summary: Appointments added through the external-calendar subscription remain on subscribers' calendars after cancellation in TendrelStep. The feed removes the event instead of emitting a cancellation entry that subscribers can process.

report.title: One insurer deposit can't be matched to multiple claims
report.description:
We received one remittance from our fictional test insurer, Vellune Cover, paying four claims together. The total equals the four outstanding claim amounts exactly, but reconciliation only lets me choose one claim for the payment. I can't select the other three or allocate portions of the same deposit across them.

Support workaround last time was to split the remittance into separate payment entries and match each one individually. That gets the claims cleared, but it turns one deposit into several entries and adds a lot of manual checking. We regularly receive these bundled payments. Can the matching screen handle one remittance against several claims without us breaking it up first?

unlisted_problem.title: Insurer remittance matching cannot handle combined payments
unlisted_problem.summary: A remittance covering several claims cannot be automatically matched to those claims. The reconciliation screen supports only one payment-to-one-claim matches, requiring staff to split the remittance manually.
